These conditions exist today and with the completion of the Downtown Expressway (the right-of-way extends the entire length of the project) they will be modified. The modification will affect the community in a number of ways and will be discussed as a separate topic in relation to the entire project area. The sum of the existing conditions in Area One can be described as deplorable, degrading, and environmentally unacceptable.
(2) Area Two shares the common boundary and environmental conditions of Meadow Street, Idlewood Avenue, and the Downtown Expressway right-of-way with Area One. With the exception of some blight "spill over" immediately west of Meadow Street the abrupt change of character is obvious. This area can be considered completely residential. Four moderately used eastwest streets (with the exception of Idlewood Avenue) intersect with four occasionally used north-south streets. Most residences front along the east-west streets. The two interior east-west streets, Rosewood Avenue and Maplewood Avenue, contain a median lined with mature and spreading shade trees. The structures are nearly a row house configuration, many sharing common walls, many having three feet separations. Most are masonary construction. Many are in good condition and are well maintained. Little clearance is warranted. Many of the structures are duplex or in some cases multi-family. The streets are narrow but can accommodate one parking lane on each side. Some litter and trash accumulation is evident in alleys but on a much smaller scale than in Area One. This area is bounded on two sides by Byrd Park and is in good balance between density and adjacent open space. The furthest area is five blocks from the park. The biggest environmental influence (other than Byrd Park) will be the Downtown Expressway.
Area Two is a conservation area. It is also an area of considerable merit and should receive immediate protection against the "spill-over" blight noted earlier along Meadow Street. Area Two is presently a pleasant residential environment but is vulnerable to the blighting influences of Area One.
